why: B (Theorem 19.6): for every compact abstract connected Riemannian ℝⁿ-manifold with any Levi-Civita connection and positive definite (blind) Ricci tensor, and ALL p, q, the blind Ω(M;p,q) (d-topology) is homotopy equivalent to a Hausdorff Mathlib CWComplex with finitely many cells in each dimension. A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric, dim ≥ 2: energy_le_of_geodesicIndex_le (the index estimate in energy form), theorem_19_6_of_ricciLowerBound (closed N, K ≥ (n−1)/r²) and theorem_19_6 (compact N, positive Ricci), both only for q NOT conjugate to p along any geodesic, with the project's countable cell-complex type (cell tower + mapping telescope) with finitely many cells per dimension. A ⇒ B fails genuinely: setting; the CW-model gap (project tower with non-cellular attaching maps vs Mathlib CWComplex: cellular approximation and the CW structure of telescopes are missing — same gap as V11_24/V10_29); and A covers only non-conjugate end points (the general case is the separate Morse.theorem_19_6_all, item V11_24). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: setting; a Mathlib CW complex does not give the project's tower; A's energy bound and the closed-N/Ricci-lower-bound variant are not in B.
